purpose: Test whether the pre-specified structural-rise idea can improve quinella ROI inside the 1-4 popularity x 5-9 popularity market skeleton.
universe: JRA flat, field size >=12, 3-win class or higher, 2024-2026 replay races with closing odds available
important_limitation: The available historical odds files contain one closing-odds row per horse, not T-15 snapshots. Therefore this is not a deployable T-15 ROI validation. Popularity ranks and quinella prices here are closing-odds proxies.

development_protocol.rule_family: Keep the high-popularity side market-based and use scenario + finishing-performance only to identify the longshot challenger.
development_protocol.challenger_definition: Closing-popularity 7-9, main-scenario rank <=3 and finishing-performance(M3) rank <=3; if multiple, choose lowest M3+scenario rank, then lowest max rank, then higher market popularity.
development_protocol.ticket: 1st favorite x one structural challenger, quinella, one point when a challenger exists

2025_2026_pooled_confirmation.interpretation: Promising but not statistically conclusive; CI crosses 1.0 because there are only 12 hits.

same_active_race_comparators.note: On 2025-26 confirmation races, the structural selector reduced three 7-9 popularity tickets to one while increasing observed ROI. The paired bootstrap ROI-difference CI still crosses zero, so this is not yet proof of superiority.

confirmation_subgroups.note: Surface and scenario splits are directionally encouraging, but grade-level samples are too small for production exclusions or overrides.

outlier_dependence.note: The result is not dependent on a single jackpot, but the top three wins are still material.

decision.next_step: Freeze this exact rule prospectively using real T-15 popularity snapshots and record the actual purchased quinella price. Do not retune the <=3 thresholds during the prospective phase.
